content.doc_md:
A stored procedure is a precompiled SQL code that can be saved and reused.

If you have an SQL query that you write over and over again, save 
it as a stored procedure, and then just call it to execute it.

A stored procedure can also have parameters, so it can act based on the parameter value(s) 
that is passed.

Stored procedures are widely used in database management, and have the following benefits:

Execute the stored procedure above as follows:

### Code Snippets

```
CREATE PROCEDURE
procedure_name
@param1 datatype
,
@param2 datatype
AS
BEGIN
-- SQL_statements to be executed
SELECT
column1
,
column2
FROM
table_name
WHERE
columnN
=
@paramN
;
END;

---

EXEC
procedure_name @param1
=
'value1'
,
@param2
=
'value2'
;

---

DROP PROCEDURE
procedure_name
;

---

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS
procedure_name
;

---

CREATE PROCEDURE 
  GetCustomersByCity
@City nvarchar(50)
AS
BEGIN
SELECT * FROM Customers
WHERE 
  City = @City;
END;

---

EXEC 
  GetCustomersByCity @City = 'London';

---

CREATE PROCEDURE 
  GetCustomersByCity
@City nvarchar(50),
@PostalCode nvarchar(10)
AS
BEGIN
SELECT * FROM Customers
WHERE 
  City = @City AND PostalCode = @PostalCode;
END;

---

EXEC 
  GetCustomersByCity @City = 'London', @PostalCode = 'WA1 1DP';
```
